As shown in Figure 8a, a steady reduction in the power conversion efficiency (PCE) is observed for temperatures above 100 °C. At the maximum curing temperature for Masterbond (80 °C), virtually no change in PCE was observed after 5 hours of annealing (Figure 8b). The experiment establishes the compatibility of Aluzine and Masterbond curing schedules; however, it is problematic for thermoplastics such as EVA that require high-temperature lamination and curing at 165 °C. Although low-temperature lamination (<90°C) may prove successful in forming an EVA-based TCC architecture on PSCs, acetic acid formation caused by EVA 17/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard decomposition has been reported to degrade PSCs. Following this initial assessment, polymer laminates (not including conductive microspheres) and TCCs (comprised of polymer matrix with conductive microspheres: Figure 9) were prepared using the Aluzine or Masterbond two-part epoxy for water vapor transmission rate (WVTR) measurements at NREL. The conductive fillers consisted of 45-53µm Ag-PMMA microspheres (Cospheric PMPMS-AG-1.53, 90% of which with diameter within the specified range) unless otherwise noted. The composite material was prepared in a glass vial by measuring the appropriate weighted ratios of the epoxy (i.e., Part-A and Part-B) and the Ag-PMMA filler, and stirred using a magnetic stir-bar for five minutes. The composite mixture was then drop-cast onto an acrylic releasing substrate (approx. 10 cm ´ 10 cm ´ 0.64 cm) and placed in a rough vacuum (approx. 0.06 bar, 15 mins) to purge air pockets introduced during mixing. To create the dispersed monolayer arrangement of the microsphere fillers within the epoxy matrix, a separate releasing substrate was introduced on the opposing side, and a compressive force applied to press the TCC mixture between the two substrates for overnight curing. Special care was exercised during the introduction of the second substrate to prevent the formation of air pockets within the composite. For the Masterbond epoxy, a secondary curing step was conducted at 60 – 80 °C for 3 – 5 hours in a furnace.
